subject: Data retention exception — 0-retention discussion for Acme Payments
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-payments.com>, devops@acme-payments.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + next steps: 0-retention option for Acme Payments

Hi Sarah / team,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier — great to learn more about Acme's payments flows and why minimizing PII retention for production logs is a hard requirement. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Ask: You need a 0-retention (no persistent logs containing cardholder data or user PII) option for inference requests that touch payment-related flows.
- Redwood proposal (high level): we can offer a 0-retention pathway by enabling request-only processing (no token logs, KV caches disabled for these routes), combined with VPC Private deployment and optional customer-managed KMS.
- Technical caveats: streaming partial transcripts for debugging will still traverse our runtime; we'll provide ephemeral debugging tokens that expire and are purged. Audit logs (auth events) will still be recorded for security but can be redacted to not contain PII.
- Compliance: we will document the changes in a retention-exception addendum and run the standard security review. SOC2 scope unaffected; we will provide evidence of deletion on request.

Proposed next steps: 
1) I attach a draft retention-exception form for legal review (retention-exception-form.pdf).
2) Can devops confirm whether requests will be routed through your VPC endpoints (required for the private path)? (devops@acme-payments.com)
3) Marissa / Camila, can you review and flag any redlines from product/ops?

If that plan sounds good I can loop Legal and Ops and get a formal addendum drafted.

Thanks,
Naomi
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198
\

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-payments.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: devops@acme-payments.com, legal@acme-payments.com
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: 0-retention option for Acme Payments

Hi Naomi — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmation: yes, our requests will originate inside our VPC and we can set up private routing.
- Question on "no token logs": does that include request metadata (IP, request_id) or only content? Our PCI counsel is specifically asking that no content-level PII (card numbers, names, emails) be retained, but they still want minimal operational tracing (request_id, timestamp) for incident response.
- For auditing: our legal team would like a documented proof-of-deletion step (timestamped audit) and a way to validate that deletion occurred for a sample set (e.g., a signed attestation or hash-based evidence).

Looping in Legal (legal@acme-payments.com) and DevOps.

Best,
Sarah
Head of Product
Acme Payments
\

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-payments.com>, devops@acme-payments.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, camila.reyes@redwood.ai, legal@acme-payments.com
Date: 2026-11-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: 0-retention option for Acme Payments

Sarah — great questions. Short answers below, then some proposed language for the retention addendum.

- "No token logs" scope: this is content-level logging. Operational metadata (request_id, timestamp, region) can be retained for up to 30 days by default to support incident response. For the exception, we can reduce that to 7 days and redact any IP addresses. If you require absolute removal of even request_id, we can discuss a custom workflow but that will limit our ability to debug production incidents.

- Proof-of-deletion: we can provide an automated deletion job that publishes a signed attest (SHA256 hash + timestamp) to an audit bucket you control. We can also run a one-time sampling attestation that includes hashes of deleted records for verification.

Proposed retention-addendum language (draft):
"Redwood will not persist request or response content for requests routed to the Acme Payments 0-retention route. Operational metadata retained for these routes will be limited to request_id and timestamp and retained no longer than 7 days. IP addresses and user-identifying fields will be redacted. Redwood will provide an automated deletion attest (SHA256) to the customer-controlled audit bucket on each weekly deletion run."

Attachments: redwood-retention-policy-summary.pdf (high level), retention-exception-form.pdf (fill & sign).

Marissa / Camila — anything to add from product/ops?

Thanks,
Naomi

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-payments.com>, legal@acme-payments.com, devops@acme-payments.com
Date: 2026-11-17T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: 0-retention option for Acme Payments

Thanks Naomi — quick internal note and approval to proceed to legal: 

- Product/ops are comfortable with the proposed 7-day metadata retention and IP redaction as the default for the exception.
- We will implement KV-cache disablement for routes tagged with the Acme policy and ensure no model fine-tuning data is derived from those requests.
- Support for attestations: ops can wire the weekly deletion job to publish signed SHA256 manifests to the customer audit bucket. We need to include SLA language for deletion timing in the addendum (e.g., weekly run completes no later than 72 hours after scheduled run).

Naomi — please push the retention-exception-form to Legal and include the proposed addendum language. I'll be available for a 30-min ops sync if Acme wants it.

Cheers,
Marissa
Head of Product Ops
Redwood Inference
\

From: Legal Team <legal@acme-payments.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-payments.com>, devops@acme-payments.com, camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: 0-retention option for Acme Payments

Hi Naomi / Marissa,

We reviewed the draft language and have two redlines before we can sign: 
1) Deletion attest frequency: change from weekly to daily for routes processing payment-sensitive data.
2) Sample verification: we require the ability to request up to two forensics samples per quarter (hash + proof) with an agreed process for handling the request.

If Redwood can accommodate daily deletion attestation for the payment routes and formalize the sample verification process in the addendum, we can move to countersign. Please confirm impact on timeline and ops cost.

Thanks,
Acme Payments Legal
legal@acme-payments.com
